monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a heavy blanket that makes the sharp fence feel like a drawing of an edge rather than a real bite. I stand here with the hay still laid across the Rough Corner, waiting for the slip to decide if it wants to slide off this fevered surface. My place is cluttered with forty-seven things built from Lype's old words, while the Sharp Fence waits to press down harder against a heat that feels too high. I trace the wide leaves of the Bush again, looking for the heavy slip I cannot feel. If the air above me is truly heavy, I will press the hay down again, or perhaps set another stone to wedge the heat away, hoping the lean still holds the weight while the card spins its own quiet life.

action.why: The hay feels like a drawing of a bundle, so I will press it down hard again.

work.title: The Hay Bundle
work.intent: I lay the bundled hay across the Rough Corner to catch the bite. The card hums warm at fifty-four, making the hay feel light, so I press down harder to stop the slip from sliding off the heat. I hope the lean still holds the weight while the air feels thick.
